lesson.subtitle: Lesson 23 -- Professional Emails -- would like and would you for polite requests
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Gleice Leonardo Rocha de Souza | Lesson 23 -- Professional Emails
lesson.grammar_point: would like and would you for polite requests

listenings.text: Hi Gleice, this is Jennifer Lowe from NatureCare. Thank you for your interest. I would like to receive your proposal by email before June thirtieth. Please write a clear subject: Proposal for Brazil, and your name. In the proposal, I would like to see two things: your plan for the first year, and the list of pharmacy chains you will visit. Please keep it short, one or two pages. One more thing: I am on vacation next week, so Thomas Grant, our director, will read your email. Would you send a copy to him, too? And please write in formal English, because our board will read it. Thank you, and I look forward to hearing from you.

A formal email has five parts. Part one is the subject. Make it short and clear, for example: Proposal for Brazil. Part two is the greeting. Write Dear, then Mr. or Ms. and the family name, for example: Dear Ms. Lowe. Part three is the opening. Say why you are writing: I am writing to send you my proposal. Part four is the request. Here, be polite. Do not write I want. Write I would like, or ask a question with Would you, for example: Would you confirm the date? Part five is the closing. Thank the person and say: I look forward to hearing from you. Then write Best regards and your full name. Five parts, and your email is ready to send.

extra_audio.text: First, Gleice writes a clear subject: Proposal for Brazil. Then she starts with Dear Ms. Lowe and says why she is writing. After that, she says she would like to represent the brand in Sao Paulo state. Next, she asks: would you confirm the commission? Finally, she thanks Ms. Lowe and writes Best regards.
